name: Igor Ter-Ovanesyan

early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv to an Armenian father who was a Soviet discus record holder and a Ukrainian mother, Ter-Ovanesyan grew up in Moscow before moving to Lviv at age 15 where he took up athletics. He was selected for the Soviet national team at age 17 and won his first Soviet title at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to an Armenian father who was a Soviet discus record holder and physical education specialist, and a Ukrainian mother; the family lived at the Institute of Physical Education dormitory.

evidence_summary: Ter-Ovanesyan's father was a Soviet discus record holder and physical education specialist, giving him direct exposure to elite athletics from childhood. He lived at the Institute of Physical Education and took up athletics at 15 in Lviv, was selected for the Soviet national team at 17, and won his first Soviet title at 19. His European Championship gold at 20 and world record at 24 confirm exceptional early achievement driven by family domain immersion and the Soviet sports pipeline.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class Soviet sports family in Kyiv; father was a Soviet discus record holder and physical education specialist, mother was Ukrainian.
